Xnergy Mandate  
1. What is Xnergy’s mission and history?  
Since 1999, Xnergy Financial (Member FINRA) has been a trusted global investment 
bank providing M&A advisory, debt and equity placement, and corporate finance 
services to emerging growth and middle-market companies. With deep expertise across 
a broad range of industries, our sector-focused team delivers tailored financial solutions 
from sell-side and buy-side M&A to capital raises and strategic advisory, with the speed

and precision that complex transactions demand. We combine the global reach of a full-
service investment bank with the personalized attention and entrepreneurial creativity 
of a boutique firm. Our clients benefit from a network of leading industry investors, 
senior-level access, and solutions built around their specific goals. Our key 
differentiator is that our work is selective, results-focused, and performance-based. 
Because our economics are tied to successful outcomes, we are intentional about 
partnering with companies where we believe we can create meaningful value. We 
measure our success by one standard: the outcomes we achieve for our clients. 
 
 
2. Which verticals are the highest priority for Xnergy and why?  
Xnergy prioritizes mature operating companies in sectors tied to services, products, 
infrastructure, or demand. These businesses fit the mandate and are less exposed to 
simple AI replacement.  
i. Business & Field Services (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, construction, 
contractors) 
ii. Technology & Digital Infrastructure (IT services, data centers, software, e-
commerce, EV charging) 
iii. AI, Media, Telecom & Cybersecurity 
iv. Healthcare & Life Sciences 
v. Manufacturing & Industrials 
vi. Financial Services 
vii. Energy 
viii. Food & Beverage 
ix. Transportation & Logistics 
x. Consumer & Retail 
xi. Aerospace & Government Contractors 
 
3. What revenue and EBITDA thresholds help define a Xnergy mandate-fit client? 
A mandate-fit client generally has >$10,000,000 in revenue or >$2,000,000 in EBITDA. 
Xnergy is focused on mature businesses that can support serious investment banking 
work, not startups in the early capital funding rounds. These thresholds help Xnergy 
focus on companies large enough to support a serious investment banking 
engagement. We also have a target minimum fee of $250,000 we would expect to 
receive on any mandate. 
 
4. What are examples of deal types that fit Xnergy’s mandate? 
Xnergy’s stated engagement scope is sell-side advisory, buy-side advisory, and capital 
raises. Venture-style startup funding rounds generally do not fit unless leadership 
approves an exception.

Outreach and Campaigns - Mark 
46. What cadence should outreach campaigns follow?  
a. Think of a five-email drip campaign as irrigation, not rain. 
b. Most prospects will not respond to the first email. A drip campaign creates a steady, 
professional sequence that keeps Xnergy visible, while providing Xnergy “surround 
sound” marketing/comms, without relying on bankers to remember every follow-up 
manually. 
c. Each email should have: 
i. Hook: why the prospect should care, benefit to them (subject line and 1st 
sentence) 
ii. Value: insight, proof, or relevance to the Prospect 
iii. CTA: one clear suggested next step 
d. Sequence: 
i. Email 1: Introduce Xnergy, explain why this prospect is relevant, ask for a short 
call. 
ii. Email 2: Share a useful industry insight or comparable transaction angle. 
iii. Email 3: Address a common objection, such as timing, valuation, or process. 
iv. Email 4: Offer a specific next step, like a 15-minute fit conversation. 
v. Email 5: Close the loop politely and leave the door open. 
e. Cadence: 1 email per week until complete. 5 week campaign. Then repeat 9 months 
later with new hooks, value, CTAs. 
f. If you want to learn more about 5 email drip campaigns, just ask Google, Co Pilot, 
Claude, ChatGPT for best practices.  
 
47. Why do most M&A and PE sourcing emails fail, and how can timing signals make 
outreach more relevant?  
a. For investment banks and private equity firms, relevance is not a persona problem. It is 
a timing problem. 
b. Most outbound sourcing fails because firms buy stale lists, filter by lazy firmographics, 
and spray the same “just checking in” email at owners who have seen that movie 50 
times. 
c. Better dealmakers hunt movement. 
d. They use outside-in signal intelligence to spot companies already in motion: leadership 
changes, capital events, SBA loans, UCC filings, licensing updates, compliance gaps, 
and Secretary of State changes. 
e. One signal is useful. Three signals stacked together become a target list competitors 
missed.

f. That changes the first email. 
g. Instead of asking, “Are you interested in selling?” the banker opens with proof they 
understand the company’s current trajectory. 
h. That is the difference between cold spam and relevant timing.

Xnergy Northstar H2:2026  
52. What is the Northstar goal for Xnergy in second half 2026?  
a. The Northstar goal is 17 completed mandate-fit discovery calls per month. This gives 
the team one clear operating target that connects sourcing, qualification, outreach, 
reporting, and management attention. 
 
53. What counts as a mandate-fit discovery call?  
a. A mandate-fit discovery call is a completed call with a prospect that appears to fit 
Xnergy’s target industries, financial thresholds, and deal mandate. The call should be 
substantive enough to help decide whether the opportunity deserves more work. 
 
54. What should not count toward the Northstar goal?

a. Do not count calls with companies outside Xnergy’s priority sectors list in Xnergy 
Mandate section above, below financial thresholds, outside the deal mandate, or lacking 
a credible transaction rationale. The goal is quality discovery, not activity theater. 
 
55. How should we report progress against the Northstar goal?  
a. Until there is Xnergy-wide CRM automation, find a method that works for you in a way 
you can share analytics with the team. When in doubt, ask Co Pilot / Claude / ChatGPT 
for suggestions on how. And confirm with management.

Pipeline: Qualification  
64. How do I score the quality of a seller prospect for Xnergy's mandate?

a. Score three items from 0–5: Average them. 0 is poor, 3 is average, and 5 is excellent. 
Use the best available information. A reasoned point of view is better than leaving it 
blank. 
i. Industry fit: Is the company in one of Xnergy’s priority verticals, and is it a 
mature operating business rather than an early-stage startup?  
ii. Financial fit: Does the company appear to meet Xnergy’s target size, including 
more than $10 million in revenue and more than $1 million in EBITDA? 
iii. Owner readiness: Is there evidence the owner may be open to selling, raising 
capital, or exploring options now?  
 
65. What is a Prospect Memo and why is it important?  
a. A Prospect Memo is the short written summary bankers circulate before the Finance 
Committee. It should go to the team at least 12 hours before the meeting. The goal is to 
answer the basics before discussion starts. Bankers should gather what they can before 
the discovery call, then use the call to confirm, correct, or fill gaps. This will feel 
imperfect at first. That is fine. The goal is to build the habit, ask better questions, and 
improve over the first 90 days. 
Here are the fields you should try to capture: 
i. Core fields, applies to all: 
1. Record type: seller, buyer, or investor 
2. Company name 
3. Lead source: UCC, SBA, CSLB, CDPH, DIR, ABC, CalEPA, Grata, or 
Other 
4. Lead source URL 
5. Year founded 
6. Website 
7. Main phone 
8. Address: street, city, state, ZIP 
9. Primary contact name 
10. Primary contact role 
11. Contact email 
12. Contact phone 
13. Owner contact verified: yes or no 
14. LinkedIn 
15. Mandate type: sell, raise, invest, or buy 
16. Bankers 
ii. Sell-side prospect fields: 
1. Company description 
2. Vertical, per mandate 
3. Company products/services and pricing 
4. Company’s target customers 
5. Company’s growth or exit priorities 
6. Employee count

7. Estimated revenue 
8. Estimated EBITDA 
9. Ownership type: founder, family, or private equity 
10. Location count 
11. Seller transaction target and rationale 
12. Willingness to sell now: 0–5 
13. Tax impact awareness: yes or no 
14. Mandate fit score: 0–5 
 
66. What questions should I ask during a discovery call?  
a. What are the company’s revenue, is revenue services or recurring, EBITDA, growth 
rate, churn, debt, cap structure, use of proceeds, competitive advantage, growth 
strategy, unique drivers, management background.  If they manufacture a product is it in 
house or outsourced/contract. If M&A also ask why selling, target valuation, and if 
management wants complete exit or to stay on after sale. Also ask if willing to take 
earn-out or stock exchange 
 
67. What should I do when a prospect says “not now”?  
a. Ask “what is a better time to get back with you and discuss?” Remember to check back

counsel. If counsel finds issues that cannot be resolved, the fee is refunded and the 
engagement is terminated.  
 
73. Who owns this stage? Finance Committee owns Vetting. The submitting banker brings the 
prospect forward, but the Finance Committee owns the review and decision process for 
whether the opportunity should move ahead.

any client information to potential investors.  Always include the client as they ar best 
equipped to answer questions. If you don’t know who the selling bankers are ask, if 
you’re not sure who to ask, ask management. 
 
84. What should weekly client updates include during placement?  
a. Weekly client updates should include activity logs and meaningful progress on buyer or 
investor outreach. They should help the client understand what happened, what 
responses came in, what went right or wrong, what is next, and what else is needed 
from them. Lists should be completed ahead fo the call with the client and the 
submitting banker should be prepared to update the client on the weekly activity. Activity

a. The deal manager and selling banker own Placement. This includes managing

Pipeline: Transaction  
88. How do I score the quality of a buyer / investor prospect for Xnergy's mandate? 
a. Score four items from 0–5. Average them. 0 is poor, 3 is average, and 5 is excellent. 
Use the best available information. A reasoned point of view is better than leaving it 
blank. 
i. Industry fit: Do they actively buy, invest in, or finance this type of business? 
ii. Deal type fit: Do they do this kind of transaction, such as acquisition, minority 
investment, growth capital, or debt financing? 
iii. Geography fit: Do they work in the company’s market or region? 
iv. Capital fit: Can they realistically fund the opportunity, based on check size, 
funding ability, and recent similar activity? 
 
89. How should an investor’s funding readiness be confirmed before we spin our wheels?  
You should always know the investor and do your due diligence and exercise judgement 
 
90. When should legal, compliance, or management be pulled in?  
a. When a problem is perceived, however, always start with reporting to management or 
compliance

a. All contractual documents relating to the transaction, fully executed. Must be retained

96. Why does Xnergy complete an After-Action Review (AAR), and what questions should it 
answer after closing?  
a. Xnergy completes AARs for every signed engagement, especially failed deals. The goal 
is honest learning. Capture what was planned, what happened, what worked, what 
failed, why it happened, and what changes next time. If you want to better understand 
AARs as a tool just google it. 
 
97. Who owns this stage?

discussed, and memorialized. The purpose is not box-checking. Every signed 
engagement should improve Xnergy’s system.
